seo.title: Solar cells from natural dyes
seo.description: Research at Truman State: 30 dye-sensitized solar cells made with beetroot and sumac dyes, characterized with UV-Vis, FTIR and impedance spectroscopy.

header.title: Dye-sensitized solar cells from beetroot and sumac
header.summary: Most dye-sensitized solar cells use metal-complex dyes. I tested whether dyes from beetroot and sumac could stand in for them, and tried to understand why the two behaved so differently.
header.imageAlt: A set of small dye-sensitized solar cells on glass, laid out on lab paper

sections.title: What I did
body: I designed the dye extraction experiments for beetroot and sumac, then characterized each dye: absorption with UV-Vis spectroscopy, functional groups with FTIR, and the finished cells' behavior with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).
I fabricated 30 lab-scale cells with a repeatable assembly process, so the cells stayed comparable, and measured each one's current–voltage curve under a solar simulator.

efficiency, a beetroot cell (49.35% fill factor)

body: Small numbers. The interesting part was why the two dyes differed.
Sumac cells drew more current, which I linked to stronger light absorption. Beetroot cells held a higher open-circuit voltage, which I linked to lower recombination.
